Burt Rutan. The aircraft designer and engineer who expanded the boundaries of what was aeronautically possible. Rutan pioneered composite aircraft construction, using advanced materials to reduce weight and increase efficiency. In 1982, he founded Scaled Composites, a company that designed experimental aircraft and pushed aeronautical frontiers. His most iconic achievement came in 1986 when the Voyager, an aircraft he designed, circled the world in nine days without refueling. He designed an unusual aircraft called the VariViggen, which demonstrated unconventional design principles using a canard configuration. In 2004, his engineering vision achieved another landmark when SpaceShipOne became the first privately-developed spacecraft to reach the edge of space. That same year, SpaceShipOne won the Ansari X Prize, spurring commercial spaceflight development. Throughout his career and into the twenty-first century, Rutan continued blending aeronautical and aerospace innovation in ways that redefined what aircraft could accomplish. He represents the modern evolution of the experimental aircraft tradition that test pilots like Chuck Yeager pioneered, building upon visionary aircraft designers like Howard Hughes who came before him.
